title: Set a pneumatic gripper's position switch on the real part: hold the valve override, slide it to where its LED lights
instruction: Set the gripper's position sensor so that it switches on when the jaws close on the test part, and not when they are open or close empty, then lock it with the screwdriver and move your hands away.
context: A robot's pneumatic gripper needs its jaw-position switch set on the real part before the robot runs, so that its program knows it holds a part, not an empty grip. This gripper is the robot's end effector, on a flange stand before it goes on the arm. The valve's manual override is non-locking: the jaws stay closed on the part only while one hand holds it down. The other hand slides the loose switch along its groove by pressing on its top (about 2 N) until its LED lights. The same D-M9N is fitted in every trial. The target moves with the selected block width. Scan the LED transitions to locate its working window (2 mm in the simulation). Centre the switch there so parts 1.2 mm narrower or wider still light it. Released, the jaws open and the LED must go out; closed empty it must stay out. Then push the screwdriver into the set screw and turn it. Part width and switch start change every trial.
setup: Station table in front of two YAM arms (bases 61 cm apart), overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Positions in cm: x forward from the line between the arm bases, y to the robot's left of their midpoint. (1) Gripper test stand at x 25-40, y -4: aluminium base plate 15 x 13 cm with a vertical flange plate. On it, bolted by its mounting face through an ISO 9409-1-50 adapter and lying on its back, a double-acting pneumatic parallel gripper (SMC MHZ2-40D: 40 mm bore, 30 mm total stroke, simulation housing envelope 96 x 66 x 42 mm, top face 7.3 cm above the table). Its jaws point forward (+x) and move along y, each with an aluminium finger 50 x 12 x 26 mm; open, the fingers are 60 mm apart. Two auto-switch grooves run along the body's top face; the one at y -2.6 holds the switch. (2) Auto switch (SMC D-M9N: 22.8 mm body, red indicator on its upper face, M2.5 slotted set screw at its front end in a small conical recess) loose in that groove at a start position drawn per trial. Its sensing point is fixed 6 mm from the non-cable end. (3) Test part: a steel block 30 x W x 20 mm in a nest between the fingers, W selected from 36, 40, 44, 48 and 52 mm. (4) Valve (SMC SY3120-5LZ-M5, 5/2 single solenoid, coil unpowered) on a mounting bracket at x 29, y 16.5, override button (blue, 4.4 mm) on top 5.5 cm above the table, tubed to the gripper. (5) A 2.5 mm precision slotted screwdriver (40 mm blade, red handle 15 mm across and 85 mm long) standing blade-down in a green rack block 4 x 4 x 4.5 cm at x 20.5, y -18.
scoring: Read at the end by cycling the gripper with the valve and watching the LED. 0.5: LED on with the jaws closed on the part, off with the jaws open. 0.75: also off with the jaws closed empty. 1.0 (ends the trial): also on with tolerance blocks 1.2 mm narrower and 1.2 mm wider than the part (switch within 0.4 mm of its window's middle); locked, so a 5 N push along the groove (push-pull gauge) does not move it; override released, nothing touching the switch and both hands and the screwdriver 8 cm or more from it for 1 s. 0 otherwise. Sim: LED on while the sensing point is within 1 mm of the piston magnet (magnet travel = jaw travel); locked = set screw turned 90 deg clockwise with the blade pushed in.
reset_notes: Keep the same D-M9N installed. Loosen the screw, slide the switch to the indicated start coordinate, fit the selected nominal gauge block, release the valve and return the screwdriver to its rack.
fidelity: One D-M9N on an MHZ2-40D, 30 mm total stroke. The model fixes the sensing point at 6 mm from the non-cable end. The 2 mm LED window and jaw-to-magnet travel ratio are approximations. The simulated cone guides a cylindrical tip and accepts any initial blade yaw. A real slotted screw needs blade alignment. An engagement comparison and LED calibration procedure are in the README. See README for setup and bench calibration.
run_limit: 2400 control steps (2 min at 20 Hz). The trial also ends as soon as the score reaches 1.0.
scores: Scripted reference 1.0 in 1,242 control steps. Dream-1 (seed 0) scored 0.0 at the 2,400-step limit. Locking the switch at empty closure failed the gauge checks and scored 0.0.
